outcome: pictorial blood loss assessment chart (PBLAC) score
cohort: 280 women aged 20-40 years, comprising 140 who underwent tubal ligation and 140 who used condoms for contraception, selected from a healthcare center in Rudsar, Iran.
finding: Women who underwent tubal ligation experienced significantly more menstrual irregularity, polymenorrhea, hypermenorrhea, menorrhagia, and menometrorrhagia compared to women using condoms for contraception.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was significantly associated with menorrhagia (OR=2.72, CI:1.49-4.97, P=0.001).
